nodes.label: Mass Produced Individualism
nodes.rationale: Freedom and individualism are twisted by those in control of wealth so constituents feel free without being free; internet socialisation streamlines a culture of distraction and homogeneity where everyone is made an individual in the same way.

nodes.label: Necessitarian Determinism
nodes.rationale: E1p33: things follow from God's nature with mathematical necessity, so alternate states are contradictory; freedom is redefined as acting from one's own nature, transforming rather than abolishing ethics.

nodes.label: Bullshit (indifference to truth + manipulation)
nodes.rationale: Bullshit is manipulation with complete indifference to truth; harmful because it strips the listener's ability to reason, producing a society without trust. Frankfurt takes a Kantian/social-contract duty to respect the right to reason.

nodes.label: Separating Art from the Artist
nodes.source_file: src/routes/blog/posts/On Separating the Art From the Artist and Ethical Anti-Theory.md
nodes.rationale: Author values independent thinking as a higher virtue, judging a work for what it presents rather than its backstory; condemning art is itself just signalling a competing virtue, and the public sphere now performs the theatre of ethics.

nodes.label: Ontological Weight (gravity-of-ideas)
nodes.rationale: Using the 4D-gravity metaphor with mass substituted for ideas: each idea has a weight/gravitational well representing its power; giving credence to an idea gifts it your power, and reality is a personal map of gravitational ideas formed outside the agent's will.

nodes.label: Revelation (as knowledge)
nodes.rationale: Knowledge has three branches - perception, reflection, and revelation. The author argues not for revelation's rational validity but its integrity: it is communication of souls, knowable only through embodiment and art, defended against Nick Land's order.

nodes.label: Shanzhai (copy as becoming)
nodes.rationale: Western 'exclusion and transcendence' venerates the original and museum-ises culture; Chinese 'inclusion and immanence' treats the copy as the synthesis of old becoming. The Ship-of-Theseus paradox dissolves because it is a flaw in the epistemology of originality, not reality.
